correctness.rationale: For F_{k+2}=pF_{k+1}+qF_k with integers p>=q>=2 and odd k, write A=(p+sqrt(p²+4q))/2 and B=-q/A. The Binet inverse expansion cancels its leading 1/A mode in the infinite partial-sum overshoot E_k. The next Binet mode at z_1=-q/A³ contributes positive (A-B)C(q/A³)^k(1+O((q/A²)^k)); the tail after J has leading c(A-B)A^{-J}/(A-1). Taking their ratio gives A^{J-lambda k-b}(1+O(rho^k)), so crossing occurs at floor(lambda k+b)+1 except at exponentially small near-integer phases. Quadratic conjugation proves lambda=3-log_A q irrational, and equidistribution along odd k makes such near-integer phases density zero. The cutoff difference 0<theta<1 and diagonal overshoot density w-theta follow. An exact rational independent check reproduced 119/120 phase predictions at small indices and the strict equality exception (2,2,1), not an all-index eventual identity.

originality.rationale: Komornik and Pedicini (2026, Theorem 1.3 and Remark 1.7) prove upper/lower integer cutoffs K1,K2 and, in the diagonal family, the density of interval WIDTH K2-K1=2. The submitted theorem instead determines the density-one phase of the ACTUAL minimal strict crossing J(k) for all p>=q>=2 and exact J-K1 frequencies, and thus the distinct density of actual K2 overshoots. Primary full text including Table 1, Remark 1.7, and proof Sections 4-5 was read. value.rationale: The minimal crossing index is the exact natural observable in the original reciprocal-Lucas inequality, whose prior published cutoffs could be nonoptimal. Quantifying whether K1+1 or K1+2 is needed at each typical odd index and the precise frequency of upper-bound overshoot resolves a motivated, identified sharpness problem. An exceptional initial strict-equality case is correctly isolated, not hidden, and the density result is meaningful even without an all-index classification.

limitations: No claim for even k or q=1; no uniformity p,q->infinity or effective density rate.
Finite calculations are corroboration, not a replacement for Binet asymptotic and Weyl equidistribution.
